candidate.answerReason: Pascal pairing rewrites S as 1 plus binomial coefficients with upper index 2015 and even lower indices. Modulo 2017, these coefficients reduce to 3,5,...,63, whose sum together with 1 is 1024.

methods.label: Pair neighboring binomial coefficients
methods.explanation:
Pairing neighboring terms lets Pascal's identity combine each pair into a single coefficient:
\[
\binom{2014}{2j-1}+\binom{2014}{2j}=\binom{2015}{2j}.
\]
The pairs with \(1\le j\le31\) cover all terms from \(k=1\) through \(k=62\), leaving the \(k=0\) term separately. Therefore
\[
S=1+\sum_{j=1}^{31}\binom{2015}{2j}.
\]
The upper index \(2015\) is just \(2\) less than the prime modulus, making these coefficients easy to reduce.

Write \(A\equiv B\pmod{2017}\) when \(2017\) divides \(A-B\). For an even integer \(r\) with \(2\le r\le62\), the binomial coefficient formula gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
r!\binom{2015}{r}
&=2015\cdot2014\cdots(2016-r)\\
&\equiv(-2)(-3)\cdots(-(r+1))\\
&=(r+1)!\pmod{2017}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last product is positive because it has the even number \(r\) of negative factors. Since \(2017\) is prime and every factor of \(r!\) is smaller than \(2017\), the product \(r!\) has no factor \(2017\). We may therefore cancel \(r!\) in this congruence, obtaining
\[
\binom{2015}{r}\equiv r+1\pmod{2017}.
\]
Applying this to \(r=2,4,\ldots,62\) yields
\[
S\equiv1+3+5+\cdots+63
=\frac{32(1+63)}2
=1024\pmod{2017}.
\]
Because \(0\le1024<2017\), the requested remainder is \(\boxed{1024}\), choice C.

candidate.annotationRationale: Computing the integer remainder is the task-level target. Pascal pairing is the method-specific simplification. The binomial coefficient formula supplies the products, prime factorization justifies cancellation modulo the prime, and arithmetic-series summation evaluates the resulting odd-number sum.

review.mathematicalCheck: Pascal pairing covers precisely the terms from 1 through 62. For even \(r\le62\), factorial reduction gives \(r!\binom{2015}{r}\equiv(r+1)!\pmod{2017}\); cancellation is valid because the prime 2017 divides no factor of \(r!\). The resulting 32 odd numbers sum to 1024, already a valid remainder.
